title: The Greek gift: when the bishop sacrifice on h7 works, and when it does not
outcomes: Plays Bxh7+ and finds the follow-up (Ng5+, then the queen to h5) when the conditions hold
Checks the four conditions before playing it
Declines the sacrifice when a knight on f6 or a bishop on e7 covers the squares, or when the knight cannot reach g5
Sees that a pawn move far from the king changes nothing

steps.text: The **Greek gift** is the bishop sacrifice on h7 (or h2). Bxh7+ Kxh7 drags the king out; then the knight checks from g5 and the queen joins on h5. It asks for a bishop on the b1-h7 diagonal, a knight that can reach g5, and a queen (or another piece) that can join on h5. It is a pattern with conditions, not a trick that always works.

steps.caption: White to move. Only the black king defends h7.

line.say: The bishop takes h7 with check.
The knight checks from g5 and clears the queen's diagonal toward h5.
The king goes back to g8.
The queen joins. Two white pieces now attack h7 and one black piece defends it.
Black takes the knight with the queen.

claims.statement: Bxh7+ is the engine's best move (depth 16).
Along the engine's best-defence line White ends at least 2 points ahead.
The bishop on e4 attacks h7.
Once the knight has left f3 the queen on d1 attacks h5.
After Qh5 two white pieces attack h7.
After Qh5 one black piece defends h7.

steps.text: Check four things before you play it, as a **rule of thumb**: the bishop reaches h7 and the king must take; a knight can check from g5; a queen or another piece can join on h5; and no black knight on f6 or bishop on e7 covers h7 or g5. If one is missing the sacrifice may lose a piece. In this lesson the engine check decides, not this list.

steps.prompt: Predict for each: does Bxh7+ work? Then check.

Which of the four conditions would you most likely forget to check in a game: the bishop's diagonal, the knight's route to g5, the queen's route to h5, or a defender on f6 or e7? Write the one you will check first.
